In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are no unique, value‐added growth experiences associated with cancer.
reports of growth in cancer survivors are not different in kind or magnitude from those of healthy controls.

the cancer experience does not appear to add any value to the experience of growth, as it is not significantly more prevalent in the cancer population than the healthy population, nor is it significantly more prevalent in those diagnosed with cancer than in those who are treated for other medical illnesses, or in those who have had a serious illness or injury.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is no value‐added by cancer.
the nature and magnitude (but not frequency) of reports of growth are unique to the experience of cancer.
there is no evidence for a unique, value‐added growth in cancer survivors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are some unique aspects to the cancer experience that may contribute to the experience of growth in cancer survivors.
the cancer experience does not appear to add unique value to growth reports.
there is no unique ‘value‐added growth’ that is specific to the cancer experience.
